遣.meaning: A queen penguin writes her orders on a flag tied to a <part>pole</part>, hands it to <part>one</part> messenger, and with a whistle in her <part>mouth</part> sends him belly-sliding down the icy <part>ramp</part> to the sea. A new order goes out every hour. She loves to <kanji>dispatch</kanji> them.
遣.on: Today's order: rescue a puppy stuck in a <sound>ken</sound>nel on a drifting ice floe.
遣.kun: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' sneezes the messenger, so she uses him again at once, to deliver a frozen <sound>ca</sound>rp.

戒.meaning: A knight guards a football <part>goal</part> with his <part>spear</part> and carves one rule into the crossbar: 'No goblin may score.' The goblins read it, gulp, and kick their ball somewhere else. Nobody breaks his <kanji>commandment</kanji>.
戒.on: One sneaky goblin tries to fly the ball in under a <sound>ki</sound>te.
戒.kun: '<sound>Ee</sound>!' squeals the goblin, and hides behind his <sound>ma</sound>ma's <sound>shi</sound>eld while the knight wags a finger: a warning.

双.meaning: Two <part>pretzel</part> twists sit side by side in a bakery window, identical down to the last salt crystal. Customers keep trying to buy just one, but the moment they're parted, both start to cry. The baker gives up: they only sell as a <kanji>pair</kanji>.
双.on: Every evening he washes them gently with <sound>soa</sound>p in the same sink, side by side.
双.kun: At night they share one tiny <sound>fu</sound>ton, curled up like two <sound>ta</sound>cos.

卓.meaning: The town's most famous plumber is up <part>early</part> every day, and the first thing he fixes is the golden <part>faucet</part> on the palace roof. Kings phone him personally, and his statue stands in three squares. He's the most <kanji>eminent</kanji> plumber alive.
卓.on: For breakfast the king serves him a golden <sound>ta</sound>co.

併.meaning: Two tiny villages each own half a rugby pitch. One night they drag their <part>rugby posts</part> together and hang both teams' scarves on one shared <part>coat hook</part>. From now on there's one team, one pitch, one song. They've decided to <kanji>join</kanji>.
併.on: The new team celebrates by building a giant goal out of <sound>hay</sound> bales.
併.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>,' sighs one village; '<sound>Wah</sound>!' cheers the other, as they put the two halves together.

葬.meaning: When the team's beloved old ball finally pops, they mourn its <part>death</part> properly: they dig a little hole in front of the <part>goal</part>, lay it inside and cover it with fresh <part>grass</part>. The coach says a few words. It's a proper <kanji>interment</kanji>.
葬.on: Afterwards everyone scrubs the mud off their boots with <sound>soa</sound>p, very quietly.
葬.kun: The groundskeeper waters the spot with his <sound>ho</sound>se, while a <sound>moo</sound>se bows its head by the fence.

宮.meaning: An old dragon's <part>spine</part> is so long that a king builds a <part>roof</part> over it and turns each bone into a room: the throne in one, the ballroom in the next, the kitchen at the tail. Visitors walk the whole backbone in slippers. It's a <kanji>palace</kanji>.
宮.on: In the games room, a prince plays pool with a <sound>cue</sound> carved from a rib.
宮.kun: A <sound>mee</sound>rkat guards the front door, knitting a <sound>ya</sound>rn flag for the roof.

催.meaning: A wealthy <part>sparrow</part> pays for the whole <part>mountain</part> bike race: she hangs the winner's jersey on a <part>coat hook</part> at the summit and has her name painted on every flag. Riders tip their helmets to her at each bend. She's proud to <kanji>sponsor</kanji> it.
催.on: Every rider gets a free cup of <sound>ci</sound>der at the finish line.
催.kun: A <sound>mo</sound>le hands out <sound>yo</sound>gurt as she holds a party at the top, and everyone cheers '<sound>Oh</sound>!'

氷.meaning: A fountain statue is spouting <part>water</part> when the cold snap hits. The whole splash freezes in mid-air, with one last <part>dot</part> of it stuck to the side like a wart. Birds use it as a perch. The fountain has become one big <kanji>icicle</kanji>.
氷.on: A skater in high <sound>hee</sound>ls spins round it, swinging a <sound>yo</sound>-yo from the frozen spout.
氷.kun: A <sound>ko</sound>ala taps it, gasps '<sound>Oh</sound>!', and slides all the way down to a frozen <sound>ree</sound>f.

傾.meaning: Everyone in the house hangs their coat on the same <part>coat hook</part> by the door, and after <part>about</part> a hundred coats the wall starts to tip. Now the floor slopes, the soup runs to one side of the bowl and the cat sleeps at an angle. The whole house begins to <kanji>lean</kanji>.
傾.on: A birthday <sound>ca</sound>ke slides slowly down the table and stops at the far end.
傾.kun: A <sound>ca</sound>lm cat, a sliding <sound>ta</sound>co and a puzzled <sound>moo</sound>se all end up in the same low corner.

浄.meaning: Two muddy kids <part>contend</part> over who gets the bathroom first, tugging a towel back and forth in the hall. While they argue, a burst pipe sprays <part>water drops</part> over both of them, head to toe. Problem solved: they're both <kanji>clean</kanji>.
浄.on: Even their pet <sound>jo</sound>ey, hiding in the laundry basket, gets a rinse.
浄.kun: Then they scrub a muddy <sound>ki</sound>wi bird and its <sound>yo</sound>-yo until both shine.

丁.meaning: A lazy city builder makes a whole neighbourhood from <part>one</part> long plank laid flat, with a <part>crowbar</part> hammered in at the end as a lamppost. Houses line up along the plank, and the crowbar's hook holds a lantern. That's the <kanji>street</kanji>.
丁.on: Under the lantern, a cat shows off a jewelled <sound>cho</sound>ker.
丁.kun: A woman in high <sound>hee</sound>ls trips on the plank, cries '<sound>No</sound>!', and grabs a <sound>to</sound>tem pole on the corner.

肌.meaning: An astronaut brings home a <part>table</part> from the <part>moon</part>, carved out of moon rock. Everyone who touches it pulls a face: it's dusty, cratered and bumpy as orange peel. Party guests can't stop rubbing its strange <kanji>texture</kanji>.
肌.on: One guest drops her house <sound>key</sound> into a crater on the tabletop.
肌.kun: '<sound>Ha</sound>!' laughs the astronaut, rubbing his cheek on it. 'Ta-<sound>da</sound>! Rough as my skin.'

罪.meaning: Grandma counts the fish in her <part>net</part>: one short. Under the table, the dog won't look her in the eye, and a <part>fishbone</part> is stuck in his whiskers. He tries to whistle. His whole face is <kanji>guilt</kanji>.
罪.on: To distract her, he bangs out a cheerful tune on a <sound>xy</sound>lophone.
罪.kun: He sneezes, '<sound>Tsu</sound>!', and the bone pings onto her plate. '<sound>Me</sound>? Never,' says his face.

謝.meaning: At the village fair, an archer means to <part>shoot</part> an apple off a dummy but pops the mayor's balloon hat instead. He drops his bow, unrolls a long <part>speech</part> on a scroll and reads every page on his knees. All he wants is to <kanji>apologize</kanji>.
謝.on: The mayor forgives him, then bats a <sound>shu</sound>ttlecock at his hat just to be even.
謝.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>,' he sighs, and knits the mayor a new hat from <sound>ya</sound>rn, the way his <sound>Ma</sound> taught him.

枚.meaning: On a hot day, a <part>tree</part> peels off a thin strip of its bark and folds it into a <part>fan</part>. It works so well that it peels another, and another, stacking them neatly on the grass like paper. Then it counts them: one <kanji>sheet of</kanji> bark, two, three.
枚.on: A crowd of <sound>mi</sound>ce sneaks off with a sheet each, to use as a blanket.

抱.meaning: A sailor tries to <part>pack up</part> his ship's <part>anchor</part> in a suitcase, but it won't fit, so he wraps both arms round it and carries it home on the bus. At the door his mum wraps both arms round him, anchor and all. A double <kanji>embrace</kanji>.
抱.on: Then she sprays the salty anchor clean with the garden <sound>ho</sound>se.
抱.kun: 'Ta-<sound>da</sound>!' he beams, and hugs the dripping anchor once more.

序.meaning: A garden <part>shed</part> hosts a snail race. <part>Beforehand</part>, a beetle in a bow tie reads out a long introduction about the history of snails, the weather and his own childhood. The snails fall asleep before the start. Nobody remembers the race, only the <kanji>preface</kanji>.
序.on: A <sound>jo</sound>gger runs past the shed and laps the sleeping snails twice.
序.kun: The beetle sneezes, '<sound>Tsu</sound>!', then adds, '<sound>Ee</sound>, by the way...', and starts a second speech.

麦.meaning: A farmer watches the weather report in the middle of his field, on a TV with a tall <part>TV antenna</part>, sitting in a <part>folding chair</part>. One summer the stalks grow so high they wrap round the antenna, and every channel shows nothing but golden, whiskery heads of <kanji>barley</kanji>.
麦.on: He loosens his belt <sound>buck</sound>le after a third bowl of soup made from it.
麦.kun: Behind his chair, a <sound>moo</sound>se and two <sound>gee</sound>se munch the stalks.

含.meaning: A tour guide shouts 'Everyone on board <part>now</part>!' and the bus door opens like a giant <part>mouth</part>: tourists, suitcases, a goat, a grandma with a cake. Nobody gets left on the pavement. The ticket is big enough to <kanji>include</kanji> them all.
含.on: Even a blob of <sound>gun</sound>k stuck to the goat's hoof gets a seat.
含.kun: Somewhere in the luggage there's a <sound>fu</sound>ton and a <sound>cu</sound>ckoo clock, both coming along.

討.meaning: A grumpy caddy wags his <part>golf club</part> like a pointer and gives a long, angry <part>speech</part> to a squirrel that has stolen three golf balls. The squirrel hangs its head, and the caddy keeps going. He's here to <kanji>chastise</kanji>, not to swing.
討.on: Halfway through the rant he drops the club on his own <sound>toe</sound>.
討.kun: '<sound>Oo</sound>!' squeaks the squirrel, and strikes back by flinging an acorn at his cap.

滑.meaning: In the haunted house, a <part>skeleton</part> mops the hall but splashes <part>water drops</part> everywhere. It takes one step, its feet shoot out, and it rattles down the corridor like a dropped bag of sticks. Haunting is hard when the floor is so <kanji>slippery</kanji>.
滑.on: It skids into the kitchen and ends up face first in a plate of <sound>katsu</sound>.
滑.kun: On the way it glides past a tray of <sound>su</sound>shi and rings the dinner <sound>be</sound>ll with its skull.

芝.meaning: The playground <part>slide</part> gets so hot in summer that the mayor glues <part>grass</part> all over it. Now kids whoosh down a green, springy chute and land on a soft mat of the same stuff. It's the only slide in town made of <kanji>turf</kanji>.
芝.on: One kid rides down sitting on a knight's <sound>shi</sound>eld, like a sled.
芝.kun: A <sound>shee</sound>p tries it too, bleating '<sound>Baa</sound>!' all the way down.

泳.meaning: A grandma enters the lake race and simply never stops: past the finish, round the island, through three winters, with <part>water drops</part> trailing off her cap. Scientists say she'll go on for <part>eternity</part>. She just loves to <kanji>swim</kanji>.
泳.on: She snacks on an <sound>a</sound>corn each lap, floating on her back.
泳.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>, hello,' she says to a passing duck, and offers it some <sound>yo</sound>gurt.

菌.meaning: A farmer finds his <part>grain</part> going green and fuzzy, so he locks the sack in a <part>cage</part> and hides it under a pile of <part>grass</part> so nobody touches it. Under his microscope, a tiny smiling blob waves back at him. It's a <kanji>germ</kanji>.
菌.on: A <sound>kin</sound>gfisher lands on the cage and refuses to eat anything near it.

罰.meaning: A pirate is caught stealing the captain's pudding. The crew rolls him up in a <part>net</part>, the captain gives a long <part>speech</part>, then points a wooden <part>dagger</part> at the mop. He must scrub the whole deck: that's his <kanji>penalty</kanji>.
罰.on: He also has to sew a missing <sound>but</sound>ton back on every coat in the crew.
罰.kun: '<sound>But</sound>, captain!' he begs, and gets an extra hour of mopping as punishment.

奏.meaning: Every winter a <part>Christmas tree</part> grows so tall it pokes into the <part>heavens</part>, and the angels use its branches as harp strings. Snow falls in time with the tune, and the stars sway. Up there, they <kanji>play music</kanji> all night.
奏.on: Far below, a crowd of kids blow <sound>soa</sound>p bubbles to the beat.
奏.kun: A <sound>ca</sound>lm reindeer taps along, using a piece of <sound>na</sound>an as a drumstick.

功.meaning: An ant drags a whole <part>workbench</part> up a hill, using every <part>muscle</part> in its six legs. At the top it plants a flag, poses for a photo and gets a medal from the beetles. It's the <kanji>achievement</kanji> of the year.
功.on: Its prize is an ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne ten times its size.
功.kun: '<sound>Ee</sound>!' squeaks the ant when the beetles add a whole <sound>sa</sound>rdine to its prize, and the crowd goes '<sound>Oh</sound>!'

融.meaning: A candy maker drops a chocolate <part>insect</part> into a <part>cauldron</part> of warm milk and watches its legs go soft, then its wings, then its little smile, until only a brown swirl is left. Stir, sip, done. Chocolate loves to <kanji>dissolve</kanji>.
融.on: A <sound>u</sound>nicorn trots in and drinks the whole cauldron in one go.
融.kun: Next she melts a chocolate <sound>to</sound>tem pole the same way.

宗.meaning: Under the <part>roof</part> of an old barn, the hens set up an <part>altar</part> with a golden corn cob on top. Every dawn they bow, cluck a hymn and lay one egg as an offering. The farmer has no idea, but his chickens have their own <kanji>religion</kanji>.
宗.on: Their holiest relic is the farmer's lost <sound>shoe</sound>, kept beside the corn.
宗.kun: A <sound>moo</sound>se peeks in, and the hens shoo it away with a <sound>ne</sound>t.
